# Anvil + Praxis demo narration

Founder voice-over draft | Final video target: exactly3:00 | 2 November 2026

Read only the quoted narration. Section labels and screen cues are for editing.
Record one continuous track with a short pause between sections, or one audio file
per section. Use your own voice; WAV or MP3 is suitable. Final screen timing will
follow the actual recording. This script does not authorize any new model run.

## 1. The problem | 0:00-0:20

Screen: Praxis and Anvil product names, then a Banking task.

“Can AI make sound business decisions under real constraints? A score alone doesn't
tell us whether it respected a bank's policy or a campaign budget. Praxis and Anvil
make that judgment explicit, testable and traceable.”

## 2. Praxis: business context and trust | 0:20-1:05

Screen: actual task authoring, evidence, constraints and rubric; label synthetic example.

“Praxis is our domain-expert task-authoring platform. Our sourcing work draws on
conversations with CMOs, SEO analysts, campaign managers, and KYC and compliance
managers at banks across geographies. Their work becomes structured tasks, rules,
rubrics and constraints.

Our production standard calls for rigorous SME onboarding and documented task review.
We intend to involve senior specialists, including retired Federal Reserve or RBI
officials where engaged, and relevant professors and guides. These verification
processes are milestones we are building, not institutional endorsements.

The aim is scale with integrity: many contributors using a consistent authoring and
review process, while preserving the business basis and provenance of every task.”

## 3. Anvil: execution and evidence | 1:05-1:40

Screen: an existing imported Banking task, pinned versions, completed run and trajectory.

“Anvil tests models against that business context. Here we can inspect the task version,
grading rules, constraints and observable actions behind a result. Frontier labs and
enterprises can investigate where models fail and identify examples for further
evaluation or their own fine-tuning and training.

Versioned task collections and repeatable execution provide the foundation for scale.
Planned compliance checks will connect requirements to legal and policy sources and
specialist review. They will support review, not automatically certify legal compliance.”

## 4. Working model results | 1:40-2:00

Screen: verified completed Astra/Claude runs and the successful Gemini diagnostic.

“Here are completed Astra, Claude and Gemini results on synthetic tasks. This Gemini
diagnostic succeeded with one real call costing less than one cent. Its generated
verifier reported one hundred out of one hundred. That result applies to this
specific synthetic trial.”

## 5. Benchmark product direction | 2:00-2:25

Screen: library → Banking comparison dashboard. Keep UI MOCKUP banner visible.

“This Benchmarks section is a UI mockup, and all displayed comparison values are
illustrative. It shows the experience we plan to build: choose a domain, compare models,
inspect coverage and failures, and trace the evaluation protocol. GDPVal is planned
and is not connected.”

## 6. The next loop | 2:25-3:00

Screen: roadmap and proposed review loop; label targets and planned integrations.

“Over the next thirty days, our priorities are remaining functionality, expert
recruitment and the review loop from Anvil into Praxis and back. We target two hundred
to five hundred expert-authored, reviewed samples per domain in Marketing, Banking
and Commerce. Beyond December, we plan Prammana and Thinking Machines integrations;
those partnerships and implementation details are not yet confirmed.

Praxis makes business expertise explicit. Anvil makes model behavior against that
expertise inspectable.”
